questions.text: What is the relative charge of a proton?

feedback: Neutrons have no charge
Electrons have a relative charge of −1

questions.solution: Protons have a relative charge of +1, electrons −1 and neutrons 0
questions.hint: Protons are the positive particles in the nucleus

questions.text: Which particle in an atom has the smallest mass?
questions.solution: An electron's mass is very small (about 1/2000 of a proton's mass)
questions.hint: Protons and neutrons both have a relative mass of 1

questions.text: What name is given to atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons? Give the term.

feedback.ions: Ions are atoms that have gained or lost electrons

questions.solution: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
questions.hint: They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers

questions.text: What are the elements in Group 1 of the periodic table called?

feedback: The halogens are in Group 7

questions.solution: Group 1 elements are the alkali metals: they react with water to form alkaline solutions
questions.hint: They react with water to make alkaline solutions

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium? Give the symbol.

feedback.S: S is the symbol for sulfur

questions.solution: The symbol for sodium is Na, from its Latin name natrium
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin name of the element, not the English one

questions.text: What are the elements in Group 0 (sometimes called Group 8) of the periodic table called?
questions.solution: Group 0 contains the noble gases, such as helium, neon and argon
questions.hint: These elements are very unreactive gases

questions.text: Where in an atom are neutrons found?
questions.solution: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons are in shells around it
questions.hint: Think about what is found in the centre of the atom

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of carbon dioxide? Give the formula.

feedback.CO: CO is carbon monoxide — carbon dioxide has two oxygen atoms

questions.solution: Carbon dioxide has one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms: CO₂
questions.hint: 'Di' means two

questions.text: Which type of bonding is found in sodium chloride?
questions.solution: Sodium chloride is made of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by ionic bonding
questions.hint: It is a compound of a metal and a non-metal

questions.text: What type of bond is formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons? Give the type.

feedback.ionic: Ionic bonding involves transferring electrons, not sharing them
feedback.ionic bond: Ionic bonding involves transferring electrons, not sharing them

questions.solution: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two atoms
questions.hint: This bonding happens between non-metal atoms

questions.text: What is the electronic structure of a sodium atom (atomic number 11)?

feedback: The second shell can only hold 8 electrons

questions.solution: 11 electrons: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second and 1 in the third — 2,8,1
questions.hint: The first shell holds 2 electrons and the second holds 8

questions.text: How does the reactivity of the Group 1 metals change going down the group?
questions.solution: Group 1 metals get more reactive going down the group
questions.hint: Compare how lithium and potassium react with water

questions.text: How does the reactivity of the halogens change going down Group 7?
questions.solution: Halogens get less reactive going down the group
questions.hint: Fluorine and chlorine are more reactive than iodine

questions.text: An atom has 17 protons and 18 neutrons. What is its mass number? Give the number.
questions.solution: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 17 + 18 = 35
questions.hint: The mass number counts the particles in the nucleus

questions.text: Which halogen is a green gas at room temperature? Give the name.

feedback.bromine: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature
feedback.chloride: Chloride is the ion (Cl⁻) — the question asks for the element
feedback.iodine: Iodine is a grey-black solid at room temperature

questions.solution: Chlorine is a green, toxic gas at room temperature
questions.hint: It is used to treat drinking water

questions.text: An atom has atomic number 8 and mass number 16. How many neutrons does it have?

feedback: 16 is the mass number (protons + neutrons)
Subtract the atomic number — don't add it

questions.solution: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 16 − 8 = 8
questions.hint: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number

questions.text: A magnesium atom loses two electrons to form an ion. What is the charge on the ion?

feedback: Atoms that lose electrons become positive

questions.solution: Losing two negative electrons leaves two more protons than electrons: Mg²⁺
questions.hint: Electrons are negative — what happens to the overall charge when they are lost?

questions.text: Name the compound formed when sodium reacts with chlorine. Give the name.
questions.solution: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl, sodium chloride
questions.hint: The name of a compound of a metal and chlorine ends in -ide

questions.text: Potassium reacts with water. Which products are formed?
questions.solution: 2K + 2H₂O → 2KOH + H₂: a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
questions.hint: Group 1 metals react with water to form an alkaline solution and a gas

questions.text: Chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution. What happens?

options: Chlorine displaces bromine, so the solution turns orange
Potassium is displaced as a solid
feedback: A less reactive halogen cannot displace a more reactive one

questions.solution: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces it: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂ (orange)
questions.hint: Compare the reactivity of chlorine and bromine

questions.text: How many electrons are in the outer shell of an atom of a Group 7 element? Give the number.
questions.solution: The group number gives the number of outer electrons: Group 7 elements have 7
questions.hint: The group number tells you this for the main groups

questions.text: Which type of structure does diamond have?
questions.solution: Diamond is a giant covalent structure: each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds
questions.hint: Each carbon atom bonds to four others in a huge network

questions.text: Why does sodium chloride have a high melting point?

options: Strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions need a lot of energy to overcome
The forces between its molecules are weak

questions.solution: In a giant ionic lattice, the strong attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions needs lots of energy to overcome
questions.hint: Think about the forces between the ions in the lattice

questions.text: Why can sodium chloride conduct electricity when molten or dissolved, but not when solid?

options: When melted or dissolved the ions are free to move
Electrons are released when it melts

questions.solution: In the solid the ions are fixed in place; when melted or dissolved they can move and carry charge
questions.hint: Which particles carry the charge in an ionic compound?

questions.text: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options: They have delocalised electrons that can move through the structure
Their positive ions are free to move
Their atoms share electrons in covalent bonds

questions.solution: Metallic bonding has a sea of delocalised electrons that move and carry charge
questions.hint: Think about metallic bonding

questions.text: An ion has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 10 electrons. What is the charge on the ion?

feedback: There are more protons than electrons, so the ion is positive

questions.solution: 11 protons (+11) and 10 electrons (−10) give an overall charge of +1
questions.hint: Compare the number of protons with the number of electrons

questions.text: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not. Why?

options: Each carbon in graphite forms three bonds, leaving one delocalised electron
Graphite contains ions that can move

questions.solution: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, so one electron per atom is delocalised and can move
questions.hint: Count the covalent bonds each carbon atom forms in each structure

questions.text: Element X is in Group 2 and Period 3 of the periodic table. Name element X.

feedback.calcium: Calcium is in Group 2 but in Period 4
feedback.beryllium: Beryllium is in Group 2 but in Period 2
feedback.aluminium: Aluminium is in Period 3 but in Group 3

questions.solution: Period 3 starts with sodium (Group 1), so Group 2 in Period 3 is magnesium
questions.hint: Period 3 starts with sodium

questions.text: Why are the noble gases unreactive?

options: They have a full outer shell of electrons

questions.solution: A full outer shell is a stable arrangement, so noble gases do not easily gain, lose or share electrons
questions.hint: Look at the number of electrons in their outer shell

questions.text: Why do Group 1 metals become more reactive going down the group?

options: The outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily
The atoms have more outer electrons
The nucleus has less positive charge
feedback: All Group 1 atoms have one outer electron

questions.solution: Further down, the single outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is lost more easily
questions.hint: Group 1 metals react by losing their outer electron

questions.text: Why do the halogens become less reactive going down Group 7?

options: The outer shell is further from the nucleus, so an electron is gained less easily

questions.solution: Halogens react by gaining an electron; further down, the outer shell is further from the nucleus
questions.hint: Halogens react by gaining one electron

questions.text: Why do simple molecular substances such as methane have low boiling points?

options: The forces between the molecules are weak
The covalent bonds inside the molecules are weak
feedback: The covalent bonds are strong and are not broken when the substance boils

questions.solution: Boiling overcomes the weak intermolecular forces; the strong covalent bonds are not broken
questions.hint: Which forces are overcome when a simple molecular substance boils?

questions.text: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his periodic table?

options: For elements that had not yet been discovered
Because some elements were too reactive
Because he ran out of space

questions.solution: He left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties, which were later found to be correct
questions.hint: He predicted the properties of some elements

questions.text: In the plum pudding model, the atom was a ball of positive charge with which negative particles embedded in it? Give the name of the particles.

feedback.protons: Protons are positive — the particles in the 'pudding' were negative

questions.solution: The plum pudding model was a ball of positive charge with electrons scattered through it
questions.hint: These negative particles had recently been discovered by J. J. Thomson

questions.text: In Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. What did this show?

options: Most of the atom is empty space
The atom is a solid ball of positive charge
Neutrons are found in the nucleus

questions.solution: Most particles were not deflected, so most of the atom must be empty space with a tiny nucleus
questions.hint: If most particles go straight through, what must most of the atom be?

questions.text: Which scientist provided the experimental evidence for neutrons in the nucleus? Give the surname.

feedback.Bohr: Bohr suggested that electrons are in shells

questions.solution: James Chadwick showed in 1932 that the nucleus contains neutrons
questions.hint: He worked with Rutherford and discovered the neutron in 1932

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
questions.solution: A neutral solution has a pH of 7; acids are below 7 and alkalis above 7
questions.hint: Pure water is neutral

questions.text: Which ions are present in all acidic solutions?

feedback: OH⁻ ions make solutions alkaline

questions.solution: Acids produce H⁺ ions in water
questions.hint: Alkalis produce OH⁻ ions in water

questions.text: What type of reaction transfers energy to the surroundings, so the temperature rises? Give the term.

feedback.endothermic: Endothermic reactions take in energy, so the temperature falls

questions.solution: Exothermic reactions transfer energy to the surroundings, e.g. combustion and neutralisation
questions.hint: 'Exo' means 'out'

questions.text: What is a catalyst?

options: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
A substance that slows down a reaction
A reactant that is used up quickly

questions.solution: A catalyst increases the rate of reaction and is not used up
questions.hint: Catalysts are not used up, so they can be used again

questions.text: What is the name of the process that uses electricity to break down an ionic compound that is molten or dissolved? Give the term.
questions.solution: Electrolysis uses a direct current to break down an ionic compound
questions.hint: It uses two electrodes and a direct current

questions.text: Which gas is produced when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid?

feedback: Carbon dioxide is produced when an acid reacts with a carbonate

questions.solution: metal + acid → salt + hydrogen
questions.hint: Write the general word equation: metal + acid → salt + ...

questions.text: What does the symbol ⇌ show in a chemical equation?
questions.solution: ⇌ shows a reversible reaction: the products can react to form the reactants again
questions.hint: The two arrows point in opposite directions

questions.text: In electrolysis, which electrode are positive ions attracted to?
questions.solution: Opposite charges attract: positive ions (cations) move to the negative cathode
questions.hint: Opposite charges attract

questions.text: In terms of electrons, oxidation is the loss of what? Give the word.

feedback.oxygen: Oxidation can be gain of oxygen, but the question asks about electrons

questions.solution: Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain of electrons (OIL RIG)
questions.hint: Remember OIL RIG

questions.text: Which salt is made when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?

feedback: Sulfates are made from sulfuric acid
Nitrates are made from nitric acid

questions.solution: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O: hydrochloric acid makes chloride salts
questions.hint: Hydrochloric acid makes salts called chlorides

questions.text: Which of these is an endothermic process?

options: Neutralising an acid with an alkali
feedback: Combustion transfers energy to the surroundings (exothermic)

questions.solution: Thermal decomposition takes in energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic
questions.hint: Endothermic processes take in energy — the others give it out

questions.text: Which metal is more reactive: copper or magnesium? Give the name.

feedback.copper: Copper is low in the reactivity series — it does not react with dilute acids

questions.solution: Magnesium is much higher in the reactivity series than copper
questions.hint: Which metal reacts with dilute acids to give hydrogen?

questions.text: Which salt is made when sulfuric acid reacts with copper(II) oxide?
questions.solution: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O: sulfuric acid makes sulfates
questions.hint: Sulfuric acid makes salts called sulfates

questions.text: What is the name for a reaction between an acid and an alkali that produces a salt and water? Give the term.
questions.solution: Neutralisation: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l)
questions.hint: The pH moves towards 7

questions.text: Magnesium is added to copper(II) sulfate solution. What happens?

options: Magnesium displaces copper, so copper metal forms

questions.solution: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it displaces it: Mg + CuSO₄ → MgSO₄ + Cu
questions.hint: Compare the positions of magnesium and copper in the reactivity series

questions.text: Which change would increase the rate of reaction between marble chips and hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution: Smaller pieces have a larger surface area, so collisions are more frequent
questions.hint: Think about surface area and the frequency of collisions

questions.text: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed. Which element is produced at the positive electrode (anode)? Give the name.

feedback.lead: Lead forms at the negative electrode (cathode)
feedback.bromide: Bromide is the ion (Br⁻) that moves to the anode — name the element it forms

questions.solution: Negative bromide ions move to the anode and lose electrons to form bromine
questions.hint: Negative ions are attracted to the positive electrode

questions.text: Copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed with inert electrodes. What forms at the cathode?

feedback: Hydrogen forms only if the metal is more reactive than hydrogen
Oxygen forms at the anode

questions.solution: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen, so copper is deposited at the cathode
questions.hint: At the cathode, the less reactive of the metal and hydrogen is produced

questions.text: Universal indicator turns purple in a solution. What is the pH most likely to be?
questions.solution: Purple shows a strongly alkaline solution, around pH 12–14
questions.hint: Purple is at the alkaline end of the colour chart

questions.text: An acid reacts with a metal carbonate to form a salt, water and which gas? Give the name.

feedback.hydrogen: Hydrogen is made when an acid reacts with a metal, not a carbonate

questions.solution: acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide
questions.hint: You can test for this gas with limewater

questions.text: Iron is extracted by heating iron oxide with carbon. Why does this work?

options: Carbon is more reactive than iron
Carbon is less reactive than iron

questions.solution: Carbon is more reactive than iron, so it removes the oxygen (reduces the iron oxide)
questions.hint: A more reactive element can displace a less reactive one

questions.text: The temperature of a reaction mixture falls from 21 °C to 15 °C. What type of reaction is this?
questions.solution: The temperature fell, so energy was taken in from the surroundings: endothermic
questions.hint: Did the reaction take in or give out energy?

questions.text: Why does increasing the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?

options: Particles move faster, so there are more frequent collisions with enough energy to react

questions.solution: Faster particles collide more often, and more collisions have at least the activation energy
questions.hint: Use collision theory

questions.text: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis, not by heating its oxide with carbon. Is aluminium more or less reactive than carbon? Answer more or less.

feedback.less: If aluminium were less reactive, carbon could extract it — it can't
feedback.more unreactive: 'More unreactive' means less reactive — if aluminium were less reactive, carbon could extract it

questions.solution: Carbon cannot reduce aluminium oxide because aluminium is more reactive than carbon
questions.hint: Carbon can only extract metals less reactive than itself

questions.text: Sodium chloride solution (brine) is electrolysed. Which product forms at the cathode?

feedback: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so it stays in solution
Chlorine forms at the anode

questions.solution: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen gas forms at the cathode
questions.hint: Positive ions go to the cathode — compare the reactivity of the metal with the other element whose ions are present

questions.text: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy of a reaction?

options: It provides a different pathway with a lower activation energy
It gives the particles extra energy

questions.solution: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy
questions.hint: Catalysts are not used up and do not change the products

questions.text: A reversible reaction happens in a sealed container. The forward and reverse reactions happen at the same rate. Give the term for this state.
questions.solution: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so the amounts stay the same
questions.hint: The amounts of reactants and products stop changing

questions.text: A solution has a pH of 2. It is diluted so its hydrogen ion concentration becomes 10 times smaller. What is the new pH?

feedback: A smaller H⁺ concentration means a less acidic solution, so the pH goes up

questions.solution: Each decrease of 10 times in H⁺ concentration raises the pH by 1: 2 → 3
questions.hint: The pH scale is a log scale: a factor of 10 changes the pH by 1

questions.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. The forward reaction is exothermic. What happens to the equilibrium yield of ammonia if the temperature is increased?
questions.solution: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) reaction, so the yield of ammonia falls
questions.hint: Which direction is endothermic?

questions.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. What happens to the equilibrium yield of ammonia if the pressure is increased?

options: It increases, because there are fewer gas molecules on the right
It decreases, because there are more gas molecules on the right
It decreases, because the forward reaction is exothermic

questions.solution: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules: 4 on the left, 2 on the right
questions.hint: Count the molecules of gas on each side

questions.text: Why is hydrochloric acid described as a strong acid?

options: It is completely ionised in water
feedback: Concentration is about the amount of acid in a volume — strength is about ionisation

questions.solution: Strong acids are completely ionised in aqueous solution
questions.hint: 'Strong' is not the same as 'concentrated'

questions.text: In the reaction Mg + Cu²⁺ → Mg²⁺ + Cu, which species is oxidised?

feedback: Copper ions gain electrons, so they are reduced

questions.solution: Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻: magnesium loses electrons, so it is oxidised
questions.hint: Oxidation is loss of electrons — which species loses electrons?

questions.text: At which electrode does reduction happen in electrolysis? Give the name of the electrode.

feedback.anode: Negative ions lose electrons at the anode — that's oxidation

questions.solution: Positive ions gain electrons at the cathode, so reduction happens there
questions.hint: Reduction is gain of electrons

questions.text: Ethanoic acid and hydrochloric acid of the same concentration react with magnesium. Why is the reaction with ethanoic acid slower?

options: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, so it has a lower concentration of H⁺ ions
Ethanoic acid has a lower pH

questions.solution: Weak acids are only partly ionised, so there are fewer H⁺ ions and fewer successful collisions
questions.hint: Compare how much each acid ionises

questions.text: Give the term for the minimum amount of energy that particles must have to react when they collide.
questions.solution: Only collisions with at least the activation energy lead to a reaction
questions.hint: A catalyst lowers this energy

questions.text: Which gas makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere today?

feedback: Oxygen is about 21% of the atmosphere

questions.solution: The atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen
questions.hint: It is not the gas we need for respiration

questions.text: What is the name for compounds made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only? Give the term.
questions.solution: Hydrocarbons contain hydrogen and carbon only, for example the alkanes
questions.hint: The name combines the two elements

questions.text: Which gas turns limewater milky (cloudy)?
questions.solution: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky
questions.hint: This is the test for the gas we breathe out

questions.text: Which test shows that a gas is hydrogen?

options: A lighted splint gives a squeaky pop
feedback: A glowing splint relights in oxygen

questions.solution: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop when a lighted splint is held near it
questions.hint: The test uses a flame

questions.text: Which gas relights a glowing splint? Give the name.

feedback.hydrogen: Hydrogen gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint

questions.solution: Oxygen relights a glowing splint
questions.hint: This gas is needed for burning

questions.text: What colour flame do lithium compounds give in a flame test?

feedback: Lilac is potassium
Yellow is sodium
Green is copper

questions.solution: Lithium gives a crimson flame
questions.hint: It is a deep red colour

questions.text: Which process separates crude oil into fractions? Give the term.

feedback.cracking: Cracking breaks large molecules into smaller ones — it does not separate crude oil
feedback.distillation: Close — crude oil needs a particular type of distillation with a column

questions.solution: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions with similar boiling points
questions.hint: It uses a tall column that is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top

questions.text: What is the general formula of the alkanes?

feedback: CₙH₂ₙ is the general formula of the alkenes

questions.solution: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, for example C₃H₈
questions.hint: Check with methane, CH₄, where n = 1

questions.text: Which homologous series contains the C=C double bond as its functional group? Give the name of the series.

feedback.alkanes: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds
feedback.alkane: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds

questions.solution: Alkenes contain a C=C double bond
questions.hint: Their names end in -ene

questions.text: Which test shows that a compound is an alkene?

options: Bromine water turns from orange to colourless

questions.solution: Alkenes decolourise orange bromine water
questions.hint: The test uses an orange solution

questions.text: What is cracking?

options: Breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones
Joining small molecules to make polymers
Separating crude oil by boiling point
feedback: That is fractional distillation

questions.solution: Cracking breaks large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes
questions.hint: It is done with a catalyst or steam at high temperature

questions.text: Which gas bleaches damp litmus paper? Give the name.

feedback.chloride: Chloride is the ion (Cl⁻) — the question asks for the element

questions.solution: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper (it may turn red first)
questions.hint: It is a green gas

questions.text: What is the name of the alcohol with two carbon atoms?

feedback: Ethene is an alkene, not an alcohol

questions.solution: Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, has two carbon atoms
questions.hint: 'Eth-' means two carbon atoms

questions.text: What colour flame do sodium compounds give in a flame test?

feedback: Lilac is potassium
Crimson is lithium

questions.solution: Sodium compounds give a yellow flame
questions.hint: Street lamps that use this metal glow this colour

questions.text: Propane, C₃H₈, burns completely in plenty of oxygen. What are the products?

feedback: Carbon monoxide forms in incomplete combustion

questions.solution: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water
questions.hint: With plenty of oxygen, the carbon is fully oxidised

questions.text: Which crude oil fraction has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution: Bitumen has the longest molecules and the highest boiling point; it is collected at the bottom
questions.hint: Longer molecules have higher boiling points

questions.text: An alkane molecule has 4 carbon atoms. Give its name.

feedback.butene: Butene is the alkene with 4 carbons — alkane names end in -ane

questions.solution: Methane (1), ethane (2), propane (3), butane (4)
questions.hint: Methane has 1 carbon, ethane 2, propane 3

questions.text: How many spots does a pure substance give on a paper chromatogram?
questions.solution: A pure substance contains only one compound, so it gives a single spot
questions.hint: A pure substance is made of just one compound

questions.text: A compound gives a lilac flame in a flame test. Which metal ion does it contain?

feedback: Sodium gives a yellow flame
Lithium gives a crimson flame
Copper gives a green flame

questions.solution: Potassium ions give a lilac flame
questions.hint: Lilac is a pale purple colour

questions.text: Poly(ethene) is made by joining many small ethene molecules. What is the name for the small molecules that join to make a polymer? Give the term.

feedback.polymer: The polymer is the long chain — name the small units

questions.solution: Monomers are the small molecules that join together to form a polymer
questions.hint: 'Mono' means one, 'poly' means many

questions.text: Which gas is made by incomplete combustion and is toxic because it reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen?
questions.solution: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, so less oxygen can be carried
questions.hint: It forms when there is not enough oxygen for complete combustion

questions.text: Why are short-chain hydrocarbons more useful as fuels than long-chain hydrocarbons?

options: They are more flammable and less viscous

questions.solution: Shorter chains ignite more easily and flow more easily
questions.hint: Compare flammability and viscosity as chain length changes

questions.text: A compound gives a green flame in a flame test. Sodium hydroxide solution gives a blue precipitate. Which metal ion is present?

feedback: Iron(II) gives a green precipitate
Iron(III) gives a brown precipitate

questions.solution: A green flame and a blue hydroxide precipitate both show copper(II) ions
questions.hint: Which metal ion gives a blue precipitate with sodium hydroxide?

questions.text: Methane, carbon dioxide and water vapour trap heat in the atmosphere. What is the general name for gases like these? Give the term.
questions.solution: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation and keep the Earth warm
questions.hint: They absorb infrared radiation from the Earth's surface

questions.text: How was most of the oxygen in today's atmosphere produced?

options: By photosynthesis by algae and plants
By the decay of dead organisms
feedback: Early volcanoes released mostly carbon dioxide and water vapour

questions.solution: Algae and plants released oxygen by photosynthesis over billions of years
questions.hint: Which living process releases oxygen?

questions.text: How is fresh water from rivers and reservoirs made potable (safe to drink) in the UK?

options: It is filtered and then sterilised
It is distilled and then cracked
It is mixed with sea water
It is boiled and then frozen

questions.solution: Water is passed through filter beds to remove solids, then sterilised (for example with chlorine)
questions.hint: Solids are removed first, then microorganisms are killed

questions.text: Ethanol is made by fermenting sugar with yeast. Which gas is also produced? Give the name.
questions.solution: Fermentation: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide
questions.hint: This gas makes bread dough rise

questions.text: On a chromatogram, ink W has spots at the same heights as dye P and dye Q only. What can you conclude?

options: Ink W contains dye P and dye Q
Ink W is a pure substance
Ink W contains every dye tested

questions.solution: Spots at the same heights (same Rf) as P and Q show that ink W is a mixture containing P and Q
questions.hint: Compare the heights of the spots

questions.text: Why do alkenes decolourise bromine water but alkanes do not?

options: Alkenes have a C=C double bond, so bromine can add across it
Alkanes are more reactive than alkenes
Alkanes have a C=C double bond

questions.solution: The C=C double bond in an alkene opens up and bromine adds to it, so the orange colour disappears
questions.hint: Think about the bonds in each series

questions.text: Why does burning fossil fuels contribute to climate change?

options: It releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that traps heat
It releases oxygen, which warms the air
It removes nitrogen from the atmosphere
It releases water that cools the planet

questions.solution: Carbon dioxide absorbs infrared radiation, increasing the greenhouse effect
questions.hint: Which product of combustion is a greenhouse gas?

questions.text: In paper chromatography, why must the start line be drawn in pencil, not ink?

options: Pencil does not dissolve in the solvent, so it does not move up the paper
Pencil lines are easier to see
Ink would make the solvent evaporate

questions.solution: Graphite is insoluble, so the line stays put; ink would dissolve and give extra spots
questions.hint: What would happen to an ink line when the solvent reaches it?

questions.text: How did the amount of carbon dioxide in the Earth's early atmosphere decrease?

options: It dissolved in the oceans and was used by algae and plants in photosynthesis
It was used by animals in respiration
feedback: Respiration releases carbon dioxide

questions.solution: CO₂ dissolved in the oceans (forming carbonates) and was taken in by algae and plants for photosynthesis
questions.hint: Think about the oceans and about photosynthesis

questions.text: Many ethene molecules join together to form a long chain. Give the name of the polymer formed.
questions.solution: Addition polymerisation of ethene makes poly(ethene)
questions.hint: Polymer names start with 'poly' followed by the monomer's name in brackets

questions.text: Why is distilling sea water to make drinking water used mainly where fresh water is scarce?

options: Distillation needs large amounts of energy, so it is expensive
Distilled sea water is too salty to drink

questions.solution: Boiling large volumes of water needs a lot of energy, so desalination is costly
questions.hint: Think about the energy needed to boil large volumes of water

questions.text: Which type of polymerisation joins monomers and also releases a small molecule such as water? Give the type.

feedback.addition: Addition polymerisation makes only the polymer, with no other product

questions.solution: In condensation polymerisation a small molecule (often water) is lost each time two monomers join
questions.hint: Polyesters and nylon are made this way
